# A prop name matched by #[wildcard] is collected into the wildcard prop under
# that prop's own name, which is what lets a component's own body read the
# value written for it. Collecting it anywhere else validates the value and
# then drops it silently: every pass downstream binds a body's prop reference
# by the declared prop's name, so the body reads the prop's zero value with
# nothing anywhere reporting the loss.
#
# The assertion is on the lowered IR rather than on markup because the static
# HTML renderer does not fold a map iteration into text — a plain map prop
# behaves the same way there, so markup could not tell the two apart.

sngl dump --stage lowered --lang none --platform html app.sngl

# The body's `data` reference became the map built from the call site, so the
# name that matched and the value written for it both arrived.
stdout 'for k, v = \{"dataRole"="row-7"\}'

# The declared prop still binds under its own name, and is not collected.
stdout 'textContent="plain"'

# The name a component-level wildcard matched reaches the declaration too:
# `vbox` renders through html.div, and `element` reads the tag it resolved to.
stdout 'tag="div"'

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:ui"
import . "sngl:macro"

component badge(
    label string = "",
    #[wildcard("data[A-Za-z0-9]*")] data map<string, string>,
) {
    text(value = label)
    for k, v = data {
        text(value = v)
    }
}

component main {
    vbox {
        badge(label = "plain", dataRole = "row-7")
    }
}
